scope: Water, rain and frost evidence for PeruRoad Climate: PE-22 Lima–Huarochiri–Yauli and Mantaro/Junin.

sources.title: Weather notice 422: precipitation in the central and southern Andes
sources.geographicScope: Central/southern Andes. Explicit potentially affected provinces include Huarochiri, Yauli, Huancayo, Concepcion, Jauja and Chupaca; exact road overlap remains uncomputed.
availableFormats: HTML notice with multiple numbered panels
Advertised WFS SHAPE-ZIP links for each forecast day; binary files not retrieved
sources.accessStatus: Notice body extracted successfully; forecast validity starts after retrieval time.
observedFacts: The exact notice 422 panel has a yellow severity level and an issue date of October 16, 2026.

It forecasts precipitation, including snow, hail, sleet and rain, for October 18–19; central-Andes rainfall forecast is 8–11 mm/day on October 18 and 9–13 mm/day for central/southern Andes on October 19.
The affected-area lists explicitly include Huarochiri, Yauli and Huancayo. Hail is forecast above 2,800 m and significant snowfall above 3,800 m.
limitations: A forecast is not evidence that rain, snow, a landslide or a closure has occurred.
Province-level inclusion does not establish that every PE-22 segment lies inside the warning polygon.
The same response includes notices 415–423; parsing the first issue date would attach the wrong date to notice 422.
Catalogue links with -prueba returned the generic institutional page; the non-prueba notice route supplied the actual numbered content.
sources.automation: Discover links in the official national notice catalogue, extract and isolate the exact notice-number panel, validate issue/start/end, archive the content and follow only actual advertised polygon links. Mark as forecast; compute polygon intersection before segment attribution.

extractionEvidence.note: Isolated the text between the headings for notice 422 and notice 423; dates and affected provinces were read from that panel.

sources.title: Historical weather notice 398: night-temperature decrease in the central and southern Andes
sources.geographicScope: Explicitly includes Junin and the provinces Huancayo, Concepcion, Jauja, Junin, Tarma, Yauli and Chupaca among other areas.
availableFormats: Advertised daily WFS SHAPE-ZIP links; binary files not retrieved
sources.accessStatus: Extracted successfully; validity expired before this research.
observedFacts: The exact notice 398 panel has a red overall severity and was issued on October 3, 2026, for October 5–7.
Its October 5 text forecasts central-Andes minimum temperatures between 0 and -6 C above 3,500 m.
The first daily affected-area list explicitly names Junin and relevant Mantaro/Yauli provinces.
limitations: This is an expired forecast, not a current frost alert or a measured frost occurrence.
Overall red severity cannot be assigned to every listed province without the daily polygons.
A separate notice 410 title also mentions the central Andes, but its extracted province lists do not include Lima or Junin; do not infer local coverage from broad titles.
sources.automation: Archive as historical forecast evidence with its original validity. A local frost alert requires a still-valid notice polygon or a timestamped station minimum observation; never reactivate this expired notice.

extractionEvidence.note: Parsed the exact notice 398 panel after the current notice panels, including the first daily affected-area list.

sources.title: Official guide to Peru hydrometeorological observations
sources.geographicScope: Peru nationwide station network. Station availability and time coverage must be checked for each PE-22/Mantaro location.
availableFormats: Linked interactive station portal; no machine-readable payload obtained
sources.accessStatus: Official guide extracted; linked station portal extracted only its station-type labels.
observedFacts: The guide describes observations of maximum/minimum air temperature, precipitation, humidity and river levels.
Conventional-station values are displayed daily; automatic-station temperature, precipitation and water-level variables are described as hourly.
It separates conventional/automatic stations and real-time/delayed transmission. Real-time conventional stations transmit at 07:00, 13:00 and 19:00.
limitations: The guide's displayed last-change date is July 30, 2020; it documents service behavior rather than proving a current station feed.
No actual Chosica, Matucana or Huancayo observation values or dates were extracted.
River level and discharge are different variables; do not convert without the station rating curve.
sources.automation: Use the linked official station portal to discover actual station metadata and payloads. Validate station identifier, coordinates, variable, unit, observation time and missing-value flags before ingestion; display unavailable until a payload is obtained.

extractionEvidence.note: Service guide body read; related station-page extraction request c3ea46ee-af5f-4604-81af-43a98c69a54b exposed only portal labels.

sources.title: Official meteorological station-data download instructions
sources.geographicScope: Meteorological stations nationwide; exact local station coverage not obtained.
availableFormats: Documented comma-separated TXT station download; actual data file not downloaded
sources.accessStatus: Instructions extracted. Download requires a registered user and the password sent by SENAMHI.
observedFacts: The official instructions document daily station files in TXT with comma-separated columns for year, month, day, precipitation type, and maximum/minimum temperature.
Registration and the emailed SENAMHI password are required before download.
limitations: This is a documented download format, not an authenticated data extraction.
No account was created and no credentials or personal information were submitted.
No public API endpoint or current measurement payload was found.
sources.automation: Use an authorized existing account for a supervised historical download and ingest the resulting TXT with explicit date/unit/missing-value validation. Do not build an unattended scraper that assumes an anonymous CSV endpoint.

extractionEvidence.note: Read the official format and registration requirements; the linked portal itself previously extracted only the page heading.

sources.title: Official accumulated-rainfall monitoring service
sources.geographicScope: SENAMHI station network nationwide; local station availability still to be checked.
availableFormats: Linked interactive accumulated-rainfall station charts; no export/API format obtained
sources.accessStatus: Official guide extracted successfully; chart data were not retrieved.
observedFacts: The service is documented as comparing the current year's daily accumulated rainfall with historical averages and historical accumulated ranges.
The guide says the information updates automatically each day and the user selects a station.
limitations: The displayed last-change date is March 13, 2023; it is not an observation timestamp.
A cumulative annual curve does not directly provide a recent 24-hour catchment rainfall amount.
No present station rainfall value or downloadable series was extracted.
sources.automation: Inspect only the linked official portal for an actual station series. Store dates and accumulation definition; derive short-window rainfall only from compatible consecutive values with valid timestamps and reset handling.

extractionEvidence.note: Read guide body and actual service link.

sources.title: CHIRILU hydrological monitoring and forecasts
sources.geographicScope: Chillon, Rimac and Lurin basins; Chosica is explicitly identified as the Rimac control station in Lurigancho, Lima.
availableFormats: Displayed forecast images and river-camera sections; no underlying numeric feed obtained
sources.accessStatus: Landing page extracted successfully; discharge table remained at a loading placeholder.
observedFacts: The page identifies Chosica as a principal Rimac hydrological control point.
The table headings distinguish today's value, historical anomaly, day-to-day trend and red threshold.
The page describes short-term flow forecasts using calibrated RS MINERVE models with ETA-SENAMHI/GFS rainfall inputs, and links a rainfall bulletin.
limitations: No live flow, river-level, anomaly or station observation time was present in the extraction; the table was still loading.
Observed flow, model forecast and camera footage require separate provenance and timestamps.
The linked PDF's age must be read inside the bulletin; the portal phrase 'last 10 days' does not establish its freshness.
sources.automation: Archive the official landing page and follow its actual bulletin link. Keep numeric observations unavailable until a timestamped station payload is obtained; ingest model forecasts separately from observations.

extractionEvidence.note: Read station descriptions, table headings, loading state, model description and exact bulletin URL.

sources.title: Official access to the National Water Resources Information System
sources.geographicScope: Peru nationwide. Rimac/Mantaro stations and downloadable series not verified.
availableFormats: Link to SNIRH portal; underlying portal extraction failed
sources.accessStatus: Official service guide extracted; actual SNIRH portal could not be fetched by Tavily.
observedFacts: ANA's official service page links to the SNIRH portal.
The documentation identifies water observatory, water-data/statistical analysis and national water-plan monitoring as services inside the platform.
limitations: A service description is not a current river measurement.
Tavily failed to retrieve the linked portal; no API, station list, download format or live Rimac/Mantaro payload was verified.
CHIRILU observatory subpages also failed extraction; their search snippets were retained only as discovery leads.
sources.automation: Use the verified official service URL as the discovery entry. Before building a collector, identify an actual accessible data endpoint or authorized download and validate metadata; expose source unavailable while the portal cannot be read.

extractionEvidence.note: Official service page read; exact SNIRH link followed in a separate failed Tavily extraction.

sources.title: ANA describes its river-flow monitoring, ONRH and ANDREA tools
sources.geographicScope: Peru nationwide; article does not supply current Rimac or Mantaro measurements.
observedFacts: The article is dated July 31, 2026 at 15:16 local time.
ANA states that ONRH disseminates levels/flows using its automatic hydrological network and interoperability with SENAMHI.
It describes ANDREA as a tool for hydrological-series analysis, inconsistency detection and data completion.
limitations: These are provider statements about system capabilities, not independently verified feed availability.
The article contains no current local observation table or documented machine-readable endpoint.
Planned interventions mentioned in the article are not evidence of road events.
sources.automation: Use as provenance for selecting the official system, then require a timestamped observation or actual downloadable data product before producing numeric water alerts.

extractionEvidence.note: Read publication timestamp and tool descriptions inside the official article.

sources.provider: INDECI / COEN, summarizing SENAMHI and CENEPRED
sources.title: Monitoring of hazards and outlooks, bulletin 290 (17 October 2026, 15:00 Lima)
sources.geographicScope: National bulletin; includes measured station rainfall at Ingenio, Concepción, Junín and warning summaries affecting Lima and Junín.
availableFormats: Official PDF and HTML archive page
sources.accessStatus: Official PDF extracted with Tavily; source is a daily report, not a live API.
observedFacts: For 16 October 07:00 to 17 October 07:00, 12.0 mm was recorded at Ingenio station, Concepción province, Junín; the bulletin classifies it as a rainy day.
It summarizes SENAMHI notice 422 for 18–19 October, including provinces in Lima and Junín, with forecast rain, hail, high-altitude snow, electrical discharges and strong gusts.
It includes daily national weather monitoring and risk summaries; each table has its own time window and geography.
limitations: The 12.0 mm value is a station observation, not rainfall on the road; the station-atlas coordinate is rounded to 0.1 degree.
Notice 422 is a forecast. The advertised shape ZIP links failed Tavily extraction and route intersection remains unverified.
The bulletin's other national summaries must not be presented as local PE-22 measurements.
sources.automation: Archive the daily PDF, parse each measurement and warning table separately, retain station/time/units and original validity, and verify published geometry before corridor attribution.
